- When sentiment shows strong positive change (e.g., +1.00 or +0.67) followed by a spike, model tends to overreact and overshoot — reduce forecast peak by 5–10%.
- If sentiment turns negative (e.g., -0.67 or below) after a rally, model often fails to adjust downward — apply downward bias of 3–8% depending on magnitude of sentiment drop.
- Model consistently overestimates prices during high-news-volume periods — reduce forecast by 1–3% for each additional news volume unit beyond 3.0.
- When sentiment change is negative and recent, model often lags — adjust forecast downward by 1–2% per day of lagged sentiment.
- Mean reversion is strong in 30-day horizon — if model is above 80% of recent 10-day average, reduce by 2–5%.
- If sentiment is neutral or flat (0.00–0.33) for 3+ days, model tends to overpredict — apply 2–5% downward correction.
- Overshoots after sentiment spikes are common — cap forecast at 10% above recent 7-day high if sentiment > 0.67.
- If sentiment is negative and news volume is low (≤2.0), model underestimates — add 2–5% to forecast to compensate for low market noise.
